test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 09 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4 i.e. Around him'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, blank number 5 is referring to where Sunny is hearing the whispers coming from. 
 
• This highlights Sunny's perception of his surroundings.
 
• 'Around him' is typically used to denote circumstances or events happening in the immediate vicinity of a person. 
 
• It also gives the image of happening on all sides around Sunny, enhancing the effect of the whispers.
 
• 'Around him' fits naturally in the sentence and doesn't change the overall meaning. It depicts a scenario where Sunny is at the center of attention because of the incident.
 
• Comparatively, 'around him' is more commonly used in English language to describe such situations when compared to the other options provided.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Option 1: Revolving him' - 'Revolving him' is not grammatically correct. The word 'revolving' generally refers to moving in a circle on a central axis, which doesn't apply to whispers or sounds.
 
• 'Option 2: Surrounding him' - While 'surrounding him' could also denote the whispers coming from all around Sunny, it feels a bit more intrusive or intense. 'Surrounding him' conveys a sense of being enclosed, which might not be the exact sense needed here.
 
• 'Option 3: Rotating him' - 'Rotating him' suggests a physical movement of Sunny, which is not what the sentence intends to convey. It's about the whispers, not Sunny's physical movement.
